newsitem.title: USA: OMB's Raines calls U.S. budget talks productive.
newsitem.headline: OMB's Raines calls U.S. budget talks productive.

text.p: U.S. Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines on Tuesday said recent meetings with Congressional leaders on balancing the budget have been productive, but they are likely to take time.

"Those discussions have been productive, informative for me, and I think a first step along a path that I hope will lead us to a bipartisan agreement to balance the budget," Raines told reporters. But he added: "Everyone informs me that he path will be longer rather than shorter. I have merely suggested that the earlier we start, no matter how long it is, we'll get it done sooner."

Raines, appointed to the OMB earlier this year when former Director Alice Rivlin became vice chair of the Federal Reserve Board, has been meeting with Congressional leaders while President Bill Clinton has been travelling in Asia.

His brief has been to try to prepare the ground for the White House and the Republican-controlled Congress to work together on balancing the budget, an effort that broke down at the start of this year ahead of the November U.S. election.

More than 50 hours of White House talks between President Clinton, a Democrat, and the Congressional leaders, who then included his election opponent former Republican Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole, ended without a deal in January.
